label: Formulated the Hermeneutics of Suspicion and narrative identity bridging sameness and selfhood
description: Ricoeur established the hermeneutics of suspicion (Marx, Nietzsche, Freud) to decipher how false consciousness and repressed desire mask truth.
historicalContext: Introduced in 'Freud and Philosophy: An Essay on Interpretation' (1965) and expanded in 'Oneself as Another' (1990).
dialecticalTension: Reconciling the archaeological critique of suspicion with the teleological recollection of meaning in narrative identity.

citations.author: Paul Ricoeur
citations.work: Freud and Philosophy: An Essay on Interpretation

label: Analyzed Freud as a master of suspicion, synthesizing energetic drives with linguistic hermeneutics
description: Ricoeur's 'Freud and Philosophy' synthesized Freud's energetic drive economics with a phenomenology of symbolic language.
historicalContext: The Terry Lectures at Yale University in 1961 published as 'Freud and Philosophy' in 1965.
dialecticalTension: Connecting the mechanical energetics of libido with the semantic interpretation of symbols and dreams.

label: Translated Husserl's Ideas I and developed pure phenomenological reduction toward hermeneutics
description: Ricoeur translated Husserl's 'Ideen I' while imprisoned in Germany during World War II, later transforming Husserlian intentionality into textual hermeneutics.
historicalContext: Ricoeur published his monumental French translation and commentary of Husserl's Ideen I in 1950.
dialecticalTension: Overcoming Husserl's ideal of immediate intuitive consciousness by insisting that self-understanding is always mediated by cultural signs and texts.

citations.author: Domenico Jervolino
citations.work: The Cogito and Hermeneutics: The Work of Paul Ricoeur

label: Extended Heidegger's fundamental ontology of Dasein into narrative emplotment and historical time
description: Ricoeur adopted Heidegger's temporality from 'Being and Time', developing it through narrative mimesis in 'Time and Narrative'.
historicalContext: Ricoeur's 'Time and Narrative' (1983-1985) directly responds to Heidegger's Sein und Zeit §72-83 on within-time-ness and historicality.
dialecticalTension: Replacing Heidegger's existential ontology of Being-towards-death with a mediated cultural narrative poetics of human acting and suffering.

label: Ricoeur's critical hermeneutics and suspicion influenced Habermas's communicative action theory
description: Habermas engaged Ricoeur's synthesis of hermeneutics and psychoanalysis in 'Knowledge and Human Interests', viewing psychoanalysis as self-reflection.
historicalContext: Habermas participated in discussions with Ricoeur on ideology critique and systematically distorted communication in the 1970s.
dialecticalTension: Communicative rational discourse free from distortion versus the inevitable historical conditionedness of textual interpretation.
